loanEmi.name: Loan EMI
loanEmi.short: Monthly payment, total interest and a full repayment schedule.
loanEmi.seo.title: Loan EMI Calculator – Monthly Payment & Amortization
loanEmi.seo.description: Calculate your loan EMI, total interest and full amortization schedule instantly. Free, private, works offline.
loanEmi.explanation: EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate (annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n is the number of monthly payments. If the rate is 0, EMI is simply P ÷ n. Each month, interest is charged on the remaining balance and the rest of the EMI reduces the principal.
loanEmi.faq.1.a: An Equated Monthly Instalment is the fixed amount you pay every month until the loan is fully repaid. It covers both interest and principal.
loanEmi.faq.2.q: Why is most of my early EMI interest?
loanEmi.faq.2.a: Interest is charged on the outstanding balance, which is highest at the start. As you repay principal, the interest portion shrinks.
loanEmi.faq.3.q: Does this include fees or insurance?
loanEmi.faq.3.a: No. Processing fees, insurance and taxes vary by lender and are not included.
percentage.name: Percentage
percentage.short: Percent of a number, percent share and percent change.
percentage.mode: What do you want to find?
percentage.explain.change.up: Going from {x} to {y} is an increase of {r}%.
percentage.explain.change.down: Going from {x} to {y} is a decrease of {r}%.
percentage.seo.title: Percentage Calculator – Percent Of, Share and Change
percentage.seo.description: Work out X% of Y, what percent X is of Y, or the percent change between two numbers. Instant and free.
percentage.explanation: X% of Y = X ÷ 100 × Y. X as a percent of Y = X ÷ Y × 100. Percent change from X to Y = (Y − X) ÷ |X| × 100.
percentage.faq.1.q: How do I calculate a discount?
percentage.faq.1.a: Use “X% of Y” with the discount as X and the price as Y, then subtract the result from the price.
percentage.faq.2.q: Why can't I find the change from 0?
percentage.faq.2.a: Percent change divides by the starting value, and dividing by zero has no meaningful answer.
